chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from a number of his companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqoub ibn Salim, raising it, said:
Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Three must not ride upon one animal, for one of them would be an Accursed'.

key_terms.يَرْتَدِفْ: to ride behind / to follow in riding

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on three people riding one animal in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of al-Kulayni’s *al-Kafi*, establishes a specific legal ruling (hukm) regarding the etiquette of riding animals, prohibiting three individuals from sharing a single beast. It attributes this prohibition to the Prophet (SAWW) via Imam Ali (AS), highlighting the spiritual consequence that one of the three riders is considered 'accursed' (ma'lun), reflecting the Shia emphasis on both physical comfort and spiritual purity in daily conduct.
